evidence_summary: July STEO supply less consumption compared with the frozen February path implies 606.171 million barrels of actual draw after separating the foregone February-forecast stock build.
accounting_interpretation: A balance residual, not a direct tank observation.
double_counting_rule: Starting identity; do not add scenario components to it.

evidence_summary: Project composite: March 129, April 117, May 73, and June minus 21 million barrels on a draw-positive convention.
accounting_interpretation: This 298 is not a cumulative figure printed in one IEA vintage; later reports substantially revised preliminary months.
double_counting_rule: Includes observed OECD government and industry stocks, visible non-OECD stocks, and oil on water.

evidence_summary: 606.171 less 298.000 equals 308.171 million barrels.
accounting_interpretation: Difference between a modeled global balance and a mixed-vintage observed-stock composite; not a measured hidden draw.
double_counting_rule: Scenario allocations below partition this row and must never be added to it.

evidence_summary: Sum of project monthly weekly-EIA changes for March through June: -4.712, 26.411, 30.837, and 14.781 million barrels.
accounting_interpretation: Included in IEA observed OECD stocks; excluded from the IEA collective-action execution headline unless a specific obligated-industry action applies.
double_counting_rule: Do not put this 67.317 into the 308.171 residual; it is already inside the 298 observed-stock composite.

evidence_summary: Sum of project monthly weekly-EIA changes for March through June: 0.377, 17.140, 40.805, and 31.464 million barrels.
accounting_interpretation: Included both in global observed stocks and, to the extent delivered under the program, the IEA collective-action execution total.
double_counting_rule: Do not add to either the 298 observed draw or the 290 collective release when using those aggregates.

evidence_summary: 89.786 million barrels of SPR draw plus 67.317 million barrels of total commercial petroleum draw.
accounting_interpretation: About 52.7% of the 298 million barrel project composite, before small IEA standardization and endpoint differences.
double_counting_rule: Memo subtotal; do not add to its two components or to the IEA observed aggregate.

evidence_summary: IEA reported a 40 million barrel March build and 41 million barrel June draw; April and May are not ownership-resolved in the public summary.
accounting_interpretation: Visible China changes are already inside observed non-OECD stocks; the known-month net says little about hidden underground movement.
double_counting_rule: Do not add the March and June observations to global stocks; they are subcomponents.

evidence_summary: Kpler estimated observable Chinese crude inventories near a record 1.24 billion barrels, up roughly 25 million since the conflict began.
accounting_interpretation: Evidence against a large visible early-war draw; does not observe underground SPR.
double_counting_rule: Already within visible-stock estimates and not additive to IEA global observed stocks.

evidence_summary: Energy Aspects, citing Kayrros, estimated almost 25 million barrels drawn from May through 7 June; Vortexa, Kpler and Energy Aspects expected about 1 mb/d draws in coming months.
accounting_interpretation: Supports a late commercial draw, but it is likely substantially captured by the IEA visible China estimate.
double_counting_rule: Do not treat as evidence for an additional 25 million hidden draw.

evidence_summary: Energy Aspects said China could allow around 1 mb/d of commercial-reserve use in April-June; FGE estimated as much as 1 mb/d in April.
accounting_interpretation: Authorization/analyst capacity, not an observed 91 million barrel draw. Later visible-tank evidence was much smaller and at times showed builds.
double_counting_rule: Context only; excluded from scenario arithmetic and observed totals.

evidence_summary: Kpler estimated Japan had cut stocks by more than 70 million barrels from a 350 million barrel pre-war baseline.
accounting_interpretation: Material but OECD-visible; it helps explain the 298 observed draw, not the 308 residual.
double_counting_rule: Do not allocate again as hidden stock.

evidence_summary: Kpler estimated a seven million barrel wartime reduction while noting possible unreported SPR activity or refinery cuts.
accounting_interpretation: Visible portion belongs in OECD observed stocks; unreported activity remains a possibility, not a quantity.
double_counting_rule: Do not add visible draw to the residual.

evidence_summary: Kpler estimated 107 million barrels at end-February and 91 million in mid-May, including SPR, commercial and refinery tanks.
accounting_interpretation: Likely within visible non-OECD stocks to the extent captured by IEA/Kpler; illustrates material refinery-stock use outside the IEA release program.
double_counting_rule: Do not automatically classify as unobserved residual.

evidence_summary: Kpler estimated ex-China Asia-Pacific stockpiles drew 78 million barrels over March-May.
accounting_interpretation: Cross-check on Japan, Korea, India and regional draws; mostly overlaps country and IEA observed-stock estimates.
double_counting_rule: Regional overlap; never add to country rows.

evidence_summary: IEA estimated oil on water swelled by 117 million barrels in June while onshore tanks drew about 96 million.
accounting_interpretation: Explains the net 21 million barrel June global build and shows why onshore-only and global-observed series diverge.
double_counting_rule: Already included in IEA global observed stocks; only measurement/timing error around it can enter the residual scenario.

evidence_summary: Published preliminary estimates moved materially: March 85 to 129; April 117 in May versus 74 in June; May 143 in June versus 73 in July.
accounting_interpretation: The 298 million barrel project figure mixes latest explicit monthly headlines rather than using a single internally consistent OMR vintage.
double_counting_rule: Zero-valued methodology memo; scenario revision allowance is separate.

evidence_summary: IEA stocks are generally primary stocks at refineries, gas plants, terminals, entrepots, pipelines and incoming vessels; tertiary/end-user and power-station stocks are excluded. Non-OECD data have no formal submission system and variable lags.
accounting_interpretation: Provides a defensible place for genuine unobserved physical draws, especially outside OECD and downstream of primary storage.
double_counting_rule: Definition memo; no quantity to add.

evidence_summary: IEA says its balancing item combines non-reported stocks, floating storage and oil in transit, plus errors in demand, supply and stock estimates; it does not force an exact balance.
accounting_interpretation: Direct official support for treating much of the 308.171 as model/coverage discrepancy rather than hidden SPR.
double_counting_rule: Definition memo; no quantity to add.

evidence_summary: Kpler found visible stocks building early and said SPR continued adding even as commercial tanks later drew; it could not rule out underground SPR transfers.
accounting_interpretation: Additional net draw not captured in visible China estimates. Base 20 is deliberately below the reported 25 million visible late draw; high 75 averages 0.62 mb/d over 121 days.
double_counting_rule: Mutually exclusive within this scenario; scenario components sum to 308.171 million barrels.

evidence_summary: IEA has no formal non-OECD stock-submission system; India and other country evidence shows commercial/refinery stocks were used.
accounting_interpretation: Net draw outside the visible-stock perimeter after removing country movements already captured by IEA/Kpler.
double_counting_rule: Mutually exclusive within this scenario; scenario components sum to 308.171 million barrels.

evidence_summary: IEA explicitly excludes tertiary/end-user and power-station stocks from its primary-stock definition.
accounting_interpretation: Physical oil consumed from stocks downstream of the primary reporting perimeter.
double_counting_rule: Mutually exclusive within this scenario; scenario components sum to 308.171 million barrels.

evidence_summary: Oil-on-water estimates swung by more than 100 million barrels and depend on cargo timing, AIS visibility and geographic classification.
accounting_interpretation: Measurement/timing difference only; the observed oil-on-water change itself is already inside the IEA total.
double_counting_rule: Mutually exclusive within this scenario; scenario components sum to 308.171 million barrels.

evidence_summary: Large month revisions and mixed publication vintages make a tens-of-millions reconciliation allowance unavoidable.
accounting_interpretation: Not a physical draw; captures IEA standardization, preliminary-to-official revisions and endpoint mismatch.
double_counting_rule: Mutually exclusive within this scenario; scenario components sum to 308.171 million barrels.

evidence_summary: Kpler said a deficit not visible in data could be underground draw or further refinery-run reductions, especially China; IEA methodology likewise leaves supply-demand-stock discrepancies in miscellaneous-to-balance.
accounting_interpretation: Demand may still be too high, supply too low, or taxonomy/timing inconsistent in the EIA vintage comparison. This is the closing model allocation.
double_counting_rule: Mutually exclusive within this scenario; scenario components sum to 308.171 million barrels.

evidence_summary: Sum of the three hidden-physical scenario components.
accounting_interpretation: Candidate physical stock draw not present in the 298 million barrel observed composite.
double_counting_rule: Memo subtotal; do not add to scenario components.

evidence_summary: Exact sum of mutually exclusive scenario allocations.
accounting_interpretation: Closes to the 308.171 million barrel project residual; not an estimate of hidden tanks.
double_counting_rule: Memo total; do not add to scenario components.
